Talukder Sarwar Hossain and another ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Dr. Shakhawat Hossain and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 2. It is necessary to state the petitioners case as stated in his application on which the present Rule has been issued. It appears that the petitioners entered into a contract for purchase of the suit property with defendant No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed through his mother Mrs. Sarwatara Begum who was appointed by defendant No. 2 as his attorney by a deed of power of attorney dated 10.6.81 to protect, preserve and manage and sell the suit property. That the said Attorney Sarwatara Begum entered into a contract to sell the suit property with the petitioner on 6.12.85 on behalf of defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed for a consideration of Taka 25,00,000.00 on receipt of Taka 10,00,000.00 as earnest money on condition that she would execute and register the sale deed within 3 months from the date of bainapatra and put the petitioners into khas possession of one of the rooms of the suit property. That thereafter Sarwatara Begum the attorney of defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed claimed more money to procure necessary document and the petitioners paid to her a further sum of Taka 5,50,000.00 against a written receipt i.e. (by endorsement made on the back side of the bainapatra) and subsequently Sarwatara Begum the attorney died on 18.8.89 before she could execute and register the sale deed. After the death of Sarwatara the attorney, defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Ahmed admitted the bainapatra executed by his mother Sarwatara Begum the attorney on 1.9.89 on receipt of a further sum of Taka 1,50,000.00 by granting a written receipt. That defendant opposite party No. 2 used to remain almost always outside Dhaka so the petitioners could not complete the sale deed in respect of the suit property in spite of their best endeavors. That the petitioners managed to meet defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed in October, 1990 and approached him to execute and register the sale deed. Defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed told the petitioners that he required one lakh taka more for obtaining income tax clearance certificate and, as such, the petitioners paid him a further sum of Taka one lac on 12.10.90 against a written receipt and opposite party No. 2 undertook to execute and register the sale deed within six months on receipt of balance of the consideration money. That thereafter the defendant opposite party No. 2 failed to execute and register the sale deed and deferred the execution and registration of the sale deed on this plea or that plea and finally on 24.10.92 refused to execute and register the sale deed by saying that the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 Dr. Shakhawat Hossain had filed a suit for specific performance of contract in respect of the suit property against him, as such, it was not possible for him to execute and register the sale deed till the disposal of the concerned suit. The petitioners thereafter on getting information slip through his Advocate came to learn from the trial Court on 26.10.92 that the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 Dr. Shakhawat Hossain had filed a suit being Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 for specific performance of contract against defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed. That thereafter on 3.11.92 the petitioners filed Title Suit No. 214 of 1992 for specific performance of a contract in respect of the suit property and for cancellation of the bainapatra of plaintiff opposite party No. 1 Dr. Shakhawat Hossain against defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed and opposite party No. 1 Shakhwat Hossain. On 4.11.92 the petitioners filed an application supported by an affidavit under sections 10 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceeding of Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 instituted by plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 Shakhawat Hossain against defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed for specific performance of a contract in respect of the suit property till disposal of Title Suit No. 214 of 1992 or in the alternative for analogous hearing of both the suits. The learned Subordinate Judge 1st Court, Dhaka by his order dated 4.11.92 stayed all further proceedings of Title Suit No. 214 of 1992 till the disposal of Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 and on the same day i.e. on 4.11.92 decreed Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 in favour of plaintiff opposite party No. 1 Dr. Shakhawat Hossain.
